title: PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent
post: We now have AI that codes and teaches itself to code better. Like hiring an intern who learns fast, except instead of leaving for a full-time offer, they evolve to take your desk.

title: Docker Sandboxes – Disposable, isolated sandboxes for AI agents
post:
Docker built a cage so AI agents can run 'YOLO mode' safely. That's the actual name for --dangerously-skip-permissions.

Your bot gets root on a fake computer where it can delete files freely. We gave robots autonomy, then immediately grounded them.

title: msitarzewski/agency-agents
post: Someone built a staffing agency for AI coding tools. Hire a frontend wizard or Reddit ninja through an app. Each agent has a personality and KPIs. We finally automated the jobs, then immediately recreated the corporate structure to manage them.

title: Over 181,000 AI meeting recordings left wide open in note taking app
post:
The AI meeting app tl;dv left 181,000 recordings exposed.

Including live calls you could simply walk into.

Researchers reported this six months ago.

The CTO hasn't responded. Too long; didn't view.

title: As AI eats the web, the internet’s collective memory is disappearing
post:
We built the internet to remember everything.

Now AI is digesting all of it into summaries, and the original pages are rotting behind paywalls and SEO sludge.

We didn't just lose the library. We replaced it with a guy who read some books once and is pretty sure he remembers.

title: Mark Zuckerberg attacks 'closed' AI rivals as Meta returns to open models
post:
The guy who made you Facebook Login to read a toaster review is suddenly passionate about open systems.

Zuck's attacking "closed" AI rivals while Meta drops free models.

Turns out "open" is easiest when it undercuts someone else's $200 subscription.

title: Go is an ideal language for AI-assisted software engineering
post:
We spent decades making code faster to write.

Now AI codes instantly, and Google says what matters is how fast you can read it.

That's their pitch for Go—boring on purpose for twenty years.
Turns out "easy to review" is the feature you need when robots are your coworkers.

title: stablyai/orca
post:
Finally got AI that codes.

Immediately started making them compete.

Orca runs your prompt across five agents side-by-side—each in their own git worktree—so you can pick the winner and merge it.

We've invented horse racing for robots, and you're the bookie.

title: AI is removing the middle class of software engineering?
post:
AI used to let bad teams ship slowly.

Now they ship instantly.

The debt just moved from "we'll fix it later" to "Claude said this works and we have no idea why it doesn't."

Turns out automating the typing just automates the mess.
